Independent Green-equation, sign and coefficient derivations; replay by differentiating the stated F and evaluating P and its derivatives at u=1/4
correctness.rationale: The bridge Green equations −g''=1 and −g''=2t−1, with zero endpoint values, give the two observation covariances u/2 and u(2t−1)/6 for u=t(1−t). Integrating against their target weights gives prior variances 1/12 and 1/180, hence normalized loss uses w=15. Gaussian conditioning gives the reduction F=u²(9+w−4wu)/[36(u+η)], with zero at deterministic endpoints. The derivative for u>0 has the sign of P=2η(9+w)+(9+w−12wη)u−8wu². For η>0 the roots have opposite signs, and for η=0 the factorization u(9+w−8wu) gives the same sign change on the positive axis. Hence the unique maximizing u is the positive root clipped at 1/4. The sign of P(1/4)=[9−w+4η(18−w)]/4 gives the full boundary and uniqueness at equality; a smaller positive u corresponds to exactly two reflected sites. The derivative of w_c is 36/(1+4η)², with endpoints 9 and limiting 18. At w=15 one obtains u_*=1/5 with no noise and the transition at η=1/2. There P_u=−126 and P_η=3, giving 1/4−u_*=(1/2−η)/42+O((1/2−η)²). Since 1/4−u=(t−1/2)², this gives the claimed displacement. The general w-boundary expansion follows from P_u=−18(1+12η) and P_w=−(1+4η)/4.
residual_risks: The independent check is analytic, not a replay of the supplied random-grid checks; those grids cannot establish global optimality. No formal verification was performed.
